title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 53 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 402–407 (Night 53, continuing directly from nights-52), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 53 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharkān, jealous of his brothers' schooling, asks for and receives the governorship of Damascus; the learned men finish teaching the other children. The young Ḍawʾ al-Makān, seeing the Iraqi pilgrim caravan, slips away with his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān to make the pilgrimage and visit Jerusalem, where he falls ill and she, penniless, goes out to find work and does not return. A bath-stoker finds the sick boy and takes him in. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammākānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the fiftieth.
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-third night,
sentences.n: The night formula. The edition prints فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ as a single word, فلماكانت, and we keep it that way. The numeral is a compound ordinal, 'the third and the fiftieth', and it takes the nominative in agreement with اللَّيْلَةُ.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَالْحُكَمَاءَ لَمَّا حَضَرُوا عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ أَكْرَمَهُمْ إِكْرَامًا زَائِدًا وَأَحْضَرَ الْجَوَارِيَ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَوْصَاهُمْ بِالتَّعْلِيمِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْأَدَبِ فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-ʿulamāʾa wa-al-ḥukamāʾa lammā ḥaḍarū ʿinda al-maliki Ḥardūba akramahum ikrāman zāʾidan wa-aḥḍara al-jawāriya bayna aydīhim wa-awṣāhum bi-al-taʿlīmi wa-al-ḥikmati wa-al-adabi fa-imtathalū amrahu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the scholars and the sages, when they were-present in the presence of the king Ḥardūb, he honoured them with excessive honouring, and had the slave-girls brought between their hands, and charged them with the teaching and the wisdom and the good-breeding; and they complied with his command.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that when the scholars and sages came into the presence of King Ḥardūb, he showed them the very greatest honour, set the slave-girls before them, and charged them with teaching, wisdom, and good breeding; and they carried out his command.
sentences.n: Shahrazād takes up her stock opening, 'it has reached me, O happy king'. 'Between their hands' is ordinary Arabic for 'in front of them'. The slave-girls are presumably the pupils the scholars are to teach, but the sentence does not say so outright.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-maliki Ḥardūba
sentences.l: This is what was, of the affair of the king Ḥardūb.
sentences.i: So much for King Ḥardūb.
sentences.n: This formula closes one strand of the story, and وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ … ('and as for what concerned …') opens the next. You will meet the pair in nearly every night.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا عَادَ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ وَطَلَعَ الْقَصْرَ طَلَبَ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ فَلَمْ يَجِدْهَا وَلَمْ يُخْبِرْهُ أَحَدٌ عَنْهَا وَلَمْ يُعْلِمْهُ أَحَدٌ بِذَلِكَ فَعَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-maliki ʿUmara bni al-Nuʿmāni fa-innahu lammā ʿāda mina al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi wa-ṭalaʿa al-qaṣra ṭalaba al-malikata Abrīzata fa-lam yajidhā wa-lam yukhbirhu aḥadun ʿanhā wa-lam yuʿlimhu aḥadun bi-dhālika fa-ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi dhālika wa-qāla
sentences.l: And as for what was, of the affair of the king ʿUmar son-of-al-Nuʿmān, then indeed he, when he returned from the hunting and the chase and went-up the palace, sought the queen Abrīza and did not find her; and no one informed him about her, and no one made-him-know of that; so that grew-great upon him, and he said:
sentences.i: As for King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, when he came back from hunting and the chase and went up into the palace, he asked for Queen Abrīza and could not find her. No one told him anything about her, and no one had let him know of it, and this weighed heavily on him. He said:
sentences.n: After the long topic (وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ …) the sentence is picked up by فَإِنَّهُ, 'then indeed he'. طَلَعَ takes the palace as a direct object, 'went up the palace', with no preposition.

sentences.t: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ أَنَّ جَارِيَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْقَصْرِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِهَا أَحَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ مَمْلَكَتِي عَلَى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ فَإِنَّهَا ضَائِعَةُ الْمَصْلَحَةِ وَلَا ضَابِطَ لَهَا فَمَاعُدْتُ أَخْرُجُ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ حَتَّى أُرْسِلَ إِلَى الْأَبْوَابِ مَنْ يَتَوَكَّلُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: kayfa yakūnu anna jāriyatan takhruju mina al-qaṣri wa-lam yaʿlam bihā aḥadun fa-in kānat mamlakatī ʿalā hādhā al-amri fa-innahā ḍāʾiʿatu al-maṣlaḥati wa-lā ḍābiṭa lahā fa-māʿudtu akhruju ilā al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi ḥattā ursila ilā al-abwābi man yatawakkalu bihā
sentences.l: How does it come to be that a girl goes out from the palace and no one has known of her? For if my kingdom is on this matter, then it is lost-as-to-its-welfare and has no controller. So I have not returned to going out to the hunting and the chase until I send to the gates one who takes-charge of them.
sentences.i: How can it be that a slave-girl walks out of the palace and no one knows of it? If that is how my kingdom is run, it is ill-governed and has no one to keep it in order. I will not ride out to the hunt again until I have sent someone to the gates to take charge of them.
sentences.n: ضَائِعَةُ الْمَصْلَحَةِ joins an adjective to a following noun, 'lost in respect of its welfare', i.e. neglected, badly managed. فَمَاعُدْتُ (printed as one word) is a past form with a firm future sense, 'I shall no longer …'. يَتَوَكَّلُ بِ is 'to take charge of, to be set over'.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَدَّ حُزْنُهُ وَضَاقَ صَدْرُهُ لِفِرَاقِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtadda ḥuznuhu wa-ḍāqa ṣadruhu li-firāqi al-malikati Abrīzata
sentences.l: And his grief grew-intense and his chest grew-narrow at the separation from the queen Abrīza.
sentences.i: His grief deepened and his breast grew tight at the loss of Queen Abrīza.
sentences.n: ضَاقَ صَدْرُهُ, 'his chest grew narrow', is the usual way of saying someone is oppressed and distressed.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِوَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ قَدْ أَتَى مِنَ السَّفَرِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ وَالِدُهُ بِذَلِكَ وَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهَا هَرَبَتْ وَهُوَ فِى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ فَاغْتَمَّ شَرْكَانُ لِذَلِكَ غَمًّا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa kadhālika wa-idhā bi-waladihi Sharkāna qad atā mina al-safari fa-aʿlamahu wālidhu bi-dhālika wa-akhbarahu annahā harabat wa-huwa fī al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi fa-ightamma Sharkānu li-dhālika ghamman shadīdan
sentences.l: And while he was thus, and behold, with his son Sharkān — he had come from the journey; and his father let him know of that and informed him that she had fled while he was in the hunting and the chase; and Sharkān was grieved at that with an intense grief.
sentences.i: While he was in this state, his son Sharkān arrived home from his travels. His father told him what had happened, and that she had run away while he was out hunting, and Sharkān was deeply troubled by it.
sentences.n: The pattern is baynamā … wa-idhā, 'while … behold', and the bi- after idhā only marks what has appeared (here Sharkān). Note the Middle Arabic spelling فِى for فِي, which the edition uses often. غَمًّا شَدِيدًا is a cognate accusative, 'grieved an intense grief'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ صَارَ يَتَفَقَّدُ أَوْلَادَهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَيُكْرِمُهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika ṣāra yatafaqqadu awlādahu kulla yawmin wa-yukrimuhum
sentences.l: Then indeed the king became (one who) inspects his children every day and honours them.
sentences.i: Then the king fell into the habit of looking in on his sons every day and showing them honour.
sentences.n: صَارَ with an imperfect verb means 'began to, came to', and here it gives a settled habit.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ قَدْ أَحْضَرَ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَالْحُكَمَاءَ لِيُعَلِّمُوا الْعِلْمَ لِأَوْلَادِهِ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمُ الرَّوَاتِبَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-maliku ʿUmaru bnu al-Nuʿmāni qad aḥḍara al-ʿulamāʾa wa-al-ḥukamāʾa li-yuʿallimū al-ʿilma li-awlādihi wa-rattaba lahumu al-rawātiba
sentences.l: And the king ʿUmar son-of-al-Nuʿmān had brought the scholars and the sages so that they might teach the knowledge to his children, and had appointed for them the stipends.
sentences.i: Now King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān had summoned scholars and sages to teach learning to his sons, and had settled stipends upon them.
sentences.n: wa-kāna … qad + perfect is the pluperfect: the king 'had' already done this. These are the scholars who were brought in at the start of the night.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ شَرْكَانُ غَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا وَحَسَدَ إِخْوَتَهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ ظَهَرَ أَثَرُ الْغَيْظِ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ مُتَمَرِّضًا بِسَبَبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā dhālika Sharkānu ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan wa-ḥasada ikhwatahu ʿalā dhālika ilā an ẓahara atharu al-ghayẓi fī wajhihi wa-lam yazal mutamarriḍan bi-sababi hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: And when Sharkān saw that, he became-angry an intense anger and envied his brothers over that, until the trace of the rage appeared in his face; and he did not cease being ailing because of this affair.
sentences.i: When Sharkān saw this, he was seized with fury and envied his brothers for it, until the mark of his rage showed on his face, and he went on pining on account of the whole business.
sentences.n: مُتَمَرِّضًا is a reflexive form of the verb 'to be ill'. It can mean 'ailing' or 'making oneself out to be ill', and the story leaves it open whether his sickness is real or put on. Sharkān speaks of a real sickness in the next lines. وَلَمْ يَزَلْ + accusative participle is 'he kept on being …'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَالِدُهُ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ مَالِي أَرَالَ تَزْدَادُ ضَعْفًا فِي جِسْمِكَ وَصُفَارًا فِي لَوْنِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wālidhu yawman mina al-ayyāmi mālī arāla tazdādu ḍaʿfan fī jismika wa-ṣufāran fī lawnika
sentences.l: So his father said to him one day of the days: What is-to-me (that) I-see-?-you increase in weakness in your body and in yellowness in your colour?
sentences.i: One day his father said to him: Why is it that I see you growing weaker in body and sallower in complexion?
sentences.n: ارال is a puzzle. The sense calls for أَرَاكَ, 'I see you', and the printed lām looks like a misprint for kāf, though it could be a slip of the pen. We vocalize the letters as printed and translate the sense. مَالِي أَرَاكَ is the stock way to ask 'why do I see you …?', and يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ is 'one day'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ شَرْكَانُ يَا وَالِدِي كُلَّمَا رَأَيْتُكَ تُقَرِّبُ إِخْوَتِي وَتُحْسِنُ إِلَيْهِمْ يَحْصُلُ عِنْدِي حَسَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Sharkānu yā wālidī kullamā raʾaytuka tuqarribu ikhwatī wa-tuḥsinu ilayhim yaḥṣulu ʿindī ḥasadun
sentences.l: So Sharkān said to him: O my father, whenever I see you drawing-near my brothers and doing-good to them, there comes-about with me an envy.
sentences.i: Sharkān said to him: Father, whenever I see you drawing my brothers close and showering kindness on them, envy takes hold of me.
sentences.n: The edition prints a shadda on تقرّب (tuqarribu, 'you bring near'), and we keep it. يَحْصُلُ عِنْدِي حَسَدٌ, 'envy occurs with me', is how Arabic says 'I feel envy'.

sentences.t: وَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَزِيدَ بِي الْحَسَدُ فَأَقْتُلَهُمْ وَتَقْتُلَنِي أَنْتَ بِسَبَبِهِمْ إِذَا أَنَا قَتَلْتُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-akhāfu an yazīda bī al-ḥasadu fa-aqtulahum wa-taqtulanī anta bi-sababihim idhā anā qataltuhum
sentences.l: And I fear that the envy increase in me, so that I kill them and you kill me on account of them, if I have killed them.
sentences.i: And I am afraid the envy will grow in me until I kill them, and then you would have me killed on their account, for having killed them.
sentences.n: The print is unpointed, and we read فَأَقْتُلَهُمْ وَتَقْتُلَنِي as subjunctives continuing أَنْ ('that … so that I kill them and you kill me'). One could instead point them as plain imperfects; the sense hardly changes.

sentences.t: فَمَرَضُ جِسْمِي وَتَغَيُّرُ لَوْنِي بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-maraḍu jismī wa-taghayyuru lawnī bi-sababi dhālika
sentences.l: So the sickness of my body and the changing of my colour are because of that.
sentences.i: That is why my body is sick and my colour has changed.
sentences.n: The edition prints a ḍamma on مَرَضُ, and we keep it. It shows this is the noun 'sickness' as subject of a sentence with no verb, 'the sickness … is because of that', and not the verb فَمَرِضَ, 'then my body fell ill'.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَنَا أَشْتَهِي مِنْ إِحْسَانِكَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَنِي قَلْعَةً فِى الْخَارِجِ مِنَ الْقِلَاعِ أُقِيمُ بِهَا بَقِيَّةَ عُمْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākin anā ashtahī min iḥsānika an tuʿṭiyanī qalʿatan fī al-khāriji mina al-qilāʿi uqīmu bihā baqiyyata ʿumrī
sentences.l: But I desire of your beneficence that you give me a fortress in the outside of the fortresses, I dwell in it the remainder of my life.
sentences.i: But what I long for, of your kindness, is that you give me a fortress, one of the outlying ones, where I can live out the rest of my days.
sentences.n: فِى الْخَارِجِ مِنَ الْقِلَاعِ is literally 'in the outside of the fortresses', meaning one of the distant, outlying forts. أُقِيمُ بِهَا, 'I dwell in it', describes the indefinite قَلْعَةً directly, with no relative pronoun.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ صَاحِبَ الْمَثَلِ يَقُولُ بُعْدِي عَنْ حَبِيبِي أَحْسَنُ لِي وَأَجْمَلُ عَيْنٌ لَا تَنْظُرُ وَقَلْبٌ لَا يَحْزَنُ
sentences.tr: fa-inna ṣāḥiba al-mathali yaqūlu buʿdī ʿan ḥabībī aḥsanu lī wa-ajmalu ʿaynun lā tanẓuru wa-qalbun lā yaḥzanu
sentences.l: For indeed the owner-of-the-proverb says: My distance from my beloved is better for me and fairer — an eye that does not look and a heart that does not grieve.
sentences.i: For the proverb says: It is better and fairer for me to be far from my beloved, with an eye that does not look and a heart that does not grieve.
sentences.n: The saying is close kin to 'out of sight, out of mind'. The last two phrases are not joined to the rest by a verb, and read as the benefit of being apart. صَاحِبُ الْمَثَلِ, 'the owner of the proverb', is the speaker the proverb comes from.

sentences.t: وَأَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: wa-aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: And he bowed with his head to the ground.
sentences.i: And he bowed his head to the ground.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ كَلَامَهُ عَرَفَ سَبَبَ مَا هُوَ فِيهِ مِنَ التَّقْصِيرِ فَأَخَذَ بِخَاطِرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku ʿUmaru bnu al-Nuʿmāni kalāmahu ʿarafa sababa mā huwa fīhi mina al-taqṣīri fa-akhadha bi-khāṭirihi
sentences.l: And when the king ʿUmar son-of-al-Nuʿmān heard his speech, he knew the cause of what he was in, of the falling-short; so he took by his heart.
sentences.i: When King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān heard his words, he understood the cause of the slump Sharkān was in, and set about soothing him.
sentences.n: التَّقْصِيرِ is 'falling short'. It may mean Sharkān's own sagging condition, or the slight he felt at his father's neglect, and the Arabic does not choose. أَخَذَ بِخَاطِرِهِ, 'took him by his heart', is an idiom for comforting someone and winning him round.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي إِنِّي أُجِيبُكَ لِذَلِكَ وَأَنَا مَا فِي مُلْكِي أَكْبَرُ مِنْ قَلْعَةِ دِمَشْقَ فَقَدْ مَلَّكْتُهَا لَكَ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā waladī innī ujībuka li-dhālika wa-anā mā fī mulkī akbaru min qalʿati Dimashqa fa-qad mallaktuhā laka min hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my son, I answer you to that; and I — there is nothing in my kingdom greater than the fortress of Damascus — so I have made-it-a-possession for you, from this time.
sentences.i: He said to him: My son, I grant you your wish. There is nothing in my realm greater than the citadel of Damascus, and I make it yours from this very moment.
sentences.n: أُجِيبُكَ لِذَلِكَ, 'I answer you to that', has li- marking what is being answered. The citadel of Damascus here stands for the whole city and its province, as the next sentence shows.

sentences.t: وَأَحْضَرَ الْمُوَقِّعِينَ فِى الْوَقْتِ وَالسَّاعَةِ وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِكِتَابَةِ تَقْلِيدِ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ وِلَايَةَ دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-aḥḍara al-muwaqqiʿīna fī al-waqti wa-al-sāʿati wa-amarahum bi-kitābati taqlīdi waladihi Sharkāna wilāyata Dimashqa al-Shāmi
sentences.l: And he had the signers brought, at the time and the hour, and ordered them with the writing of the investiture of his son Sharkān with the governorship of Damascus of-the-Levant.
sentences.i: He summoned the secretaries then and there and commanded them to draw up the patent investing his son Sharkān with the governorship of Damascus in Syria.
sentences.n: The edition prints a shadda on الْمُوَقِّعِين, the secretaries who sign and endorse official documents, and we keep it. فِى الْوَقْتِ وَالسَّاعَةِ, 'at the time and the hour', means 'on the spot'. أَمَرَ بِ is the verb's own preposition, 'order (someone to do) …'. الشَّام is Syria.

sentences.t: فَكَتَبُوا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَجَهَّزُوهُ وَأَخَدَ مَعَهُ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-katabū lahu dhālika wa-jahhazūhu wa-akhada maʿahu al-wazīra Dandāna
sentences.l: So they wrote for him that, and equipped him, and he took with him the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: They wrote it out for him and fitted him out for the journey, and he took the vizier Dandān with him.
sentences.n: أَخَدَ is the edition's spelling of أَخَذَ with dāl in place of dhāl. The two sounds have merged in many speakers, and the spelling shows it. We keep it.

sentences.t: وَأَوْصَاهُ أَبُوهُ بِالْمَمْلَكَةِ وَالسِّيَاسَةِ وَقَلَّدَهُ أُمُورَهُ وَالْإِقَامَةَ عِنْدَهُ وَوَدَّعَهُ أَبُوهُ وَوَدَّعَتْهُ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَأَكَابِرُ الدَّوْلَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-awṣāhu abūhu bi-al-mamlakati wa-al-siyāsati wa-qalladahu umūrahu wa-al-iqāmata ʿindahu wa-waddaʿahu abūhu wa-waddaʿathu al-umarāʾu wa-akābiru al-dawlati
sentences.l: And his father charged him with the kingdom and the statecraft, and invested him with his affairs and the staying with him, and his father bade-him-farewell, and the emirs bade him farewell, and the grandees of the state.
sentences.i: His father charged him with the government and its management, entrusted his affairs to him and told him to stay by his side, and then bade him farewell, as did the emirs and the great men of the realm.
sentences.n: The pronouns in the middle are ambiguous. The father may be charging the vizier Dandān to run the province and to stay at Sharkān's side, or charging Sharkān himself. The idiomatic line keeps the same ambiguity. أَوْصَى بِ is 'to charge someone with'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارَ بِالْعَسْكَرِ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: thumma sāra bi-al-ʿaskari ḥattā waṣala ilā Dimashqa
sentences.l: Then he travelled with the army until he arrived at Damascus.
sentences.i: Then he marched with the army until he reached Damascus.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَيْهَادَقَّ لَهُ أَهْلُهَا الْكَاسَاتِ وَصَاحُوا بِالْبُوقَاتِ وَزَيَّنُوا الْمَدِينَةَ وَقَابَلُوهُ بِمَوْكِبٍ عَظِيمٍ سَارَفِيهِ أَهْلُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ مَيْمَنَةً وَالْمَيْسَرَةِ مَيْسَرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilayhā daqqa lahu ahluhā al-kāsāti wa-ṣāḥū bi-al-būqāti wa-zayyanū al-madīnata wa-qābalūhu bi-mawkibin ʿaẓīmin sāra fīhi ahlu al-maymanati maymanatan wa-al-maysarati maysaratan
sentences.l: And when he arrived at it, its people beat for him the cups, and cried-out with the trumpets, and adorned the city, and met him with a great procession in which the people of the right-wing went as a right-wing, and the left-wing as a left-wing.
sentences.i: When he reached the city, its people beat the cymbals in welcome, blew the trumpets, decked the town, and met him with a grand procession, in which the men of the right marched as the right wing and those of the left as the left.
sentences.n: Two words are printed run together: إِلَيْهَادَقَّ is إِلَيْهَا دَقَّ, and سَارَفِيهِ is سَارَ فِيهِ. We keep them as printed. الْكَاسَات (literally 'cups') are small cymbals or bowl-shaped drums, and صَاحُوا بِالْبُوقَاتِ, 'cried out with the trumpets', means they sounded them loudly. In the last clause we supply 'the people of' before الْمَيْسَرَةِ.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri Sharkāna
sentences.l: This is what was, of the affair of Sharkān.
sentences.i: So much for Sharkān.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ وَالِدِهِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَإِنَّهُ بَعْدَ سَفَرِ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْحُكَمَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri wālidihi ʿUmara bni al-Nuʿmāni fa-innahu baʿda safari waladihi Sharkāna aqbala ʿalayhi al-ḥukamāʾu
sentences.l: And as-for what was of the affair of his father ʿUmar son-of-al-Nuʿmān: indeed-it, after the journey of his son Sharkān, the sages approached him.
sentences.i: As for what befell his father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān: after his son Sharkān had gone away, the sages came before him
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ … is the storyteller's stock turn to a second thread: "as for what concerned …". The فَإِنَّهُ that follows picks up the clause once the long topic has been named; read it as "it was that …".

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا لَهُ يَا مَوْلَانَا إِنَّ أَوْلَادَكَ تَعَلَّمُوا الْعِلْمَ وَكَمَّلُوا الْحِكْمَةَ وَالْأَدَبَ وَالْحَشْمَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū lahu yā mawlānā inna awlādaka taʿallamū al-ʿilma wa-kammalū al-ḥikmata wa-al-adaba wa-al-ḥashmata
sentences.l: And they said to him: O our master, indeed your sons have-learned the knowledge and have-perfected the wisdom and the culture and the decorum.
sentences.i: and said to him, "O our lord, your sons have learned all knowledge and have been brought to perfection in wisdom, good breeding and dignity of bearing."
sentences.n: الْحَشْمَة is dignity, decorum, the modesty of a well-bred person. The three nouns after كَمَّلُوا make a courtly little list, and the rhyme of -ma / -ba / -ma is only faint.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ فَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَأَنْعَمَ عَلَى الْحُكَمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika fariḥa al-maliku faraḥan shadīdan wa-anʿama ʿalā al-ḥukamāʾi
sentences.l: So at that, the king rejoiced a severe rejoicing, and bestowed-favour upon the sages.
sentences.i: At this the king rejoiced exceedingly, and showered his favours upon the sages,
sentences.n: فَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا repeats the verb's own root as an accusative ("rejoiced a strong rejoicing"), a common way to say "greatly". أَنْعَمَ عَلَى is "to bestow favour (gifts) upon".

sentences.t: حَيْثُ رَأَى ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ كَبُرَ وَتَرَعْرَعَ وَرَكِبَ الْخَيْلَ وَصَارَ لَهُ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: ḥaythu raʾā Ḍawʾa al-Makāni kabura wa-tarʿaraʿa wa-rakiba al-khayla wa-ṣāra lahu mina al-ʿumri arbaʿa ʿashrata sanatan
sentences.l: Since he saw Ḍawʾ al-Makān grown-big and thriving, and he had mounted the horses, and there came-to-be to him of age fourteen years.
sentences.i: for he saw that Ḍawʾ al-Makān had grown tall and flourished, had learned to ride, and had reached the age of fourteen.
sentences.n: Here حَيْثُ means "inasmuch as, seeing that" rather than its usual "where". Ḍawʾ al-Makān is the subject of the whole run of verbs كَبُرَ وَتَرَعْرَعَ وَرَكِبَ …, which the king takes in as he looks at him. رَكِبَ الْخَيْلَ is "he rode horses", that is, he had become a horseman.

sentences.t: وَطَلَعَ مُشْتَغِلًا بِالدِّيَانَةِ وَالْعِبَادَةِ مُحِبًّا لِلْفُقَرَاءِ وَأَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ وَالْقُرْأَنِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaʿa mushtaghilan bi-al-diyānati wa-al-ʿibādati muḥibban li-al-fuqarāʾi wa-ahli al-ʿilmi wa-al-qurʾāni
sentences.l: And he came-forth occupied with the religion and the worship, a-lover to the poor-ones and the people of knowledge and the Qurʾān.
sentences.i: And he grew up devoted to piety and worship, a friend to the poor, to men of learning, and to the Qurʾān.
sentences.n: طَلَعَ is "to go up, come forth"; with a participle after it, as here, it means "he turned out, he came to be". The edition prints الْقُرْأَن with the hamza and no alif after it, so the word reads qurʾān.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ أَهْلُ بَغْدَادَ يُحِبُّونَهُ نِسَاءً وَرِجَالًا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra ahlu Baghdāda yuḥibbūnahu nisāʾan wa-rijālan
sentences.l: And the people of Baghdad became loving him, women and men.
sentences.i: and the people of Baghdad, women and men alike, came to love him,
sentences.n: نِسَاءً وَرِجَالًا are accusatives that say who the "people" were; English puts them as "women and men alike". صَارَ with an imperfect verb means "came to, began to".

sentences.t: إِلَى أَنْ طَافَ بِبَغْدَادَ مَحْمِلُ الْعِرَاقِ مِنْ أَجْلِ الْحَجِّ وَ زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: ilā an ṭāfa bi-Baghdāda maḥmilu al-ʿirāqi min ajli al-ḥajji wa- ziyārati qabri al-nabiyyi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: Until the litter of Iraq made-its-round through Baghdad, for the sake of the pilgrimage and the visiting of the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace.
sentences.i: until the Iraqi pilgrim-litter came round to Baghdad on its way to the Pilgrimage and to visit the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace.
sentences.n: The مَحْمِل (maḥmil) was the ceremonially decked litter carried at the head of the pilgrim caravan; its progress through a city announced that the Pilgrimage was setting out. The conjunction وَ stands apart from زِيَارَة in the print, and we keep them as two words. صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ is the blessing said after the Prophet's name; it is a wish, "may God bless him".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ مَوْكِبَ الْمَحْمَلِ اشْتَاقَ إِلَى الْحَجِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā Ḍawʾu al-Makāni mawkiba al-maḥmili ishtāqa ilā al-ḥajji
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw the procession of the litter, he longed toward the pilgrimage.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw the litter's procession, he was seized with longing for the Pilgrimage.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ لِا سْتَأْذِنَكَ فِي أَنْ أَحُجَّ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalā wālidihi wa-qāla lahu innī ataytu ilayka li- staʾdhinaka fī an aḥujja
sentences.l: And he entered upon his father and said to him: Indeed I have come to you to ask-your-leave, in that I go-on-pilgrimage.
sentences.i: He went in to his father and said, "I have come to ask your leave to go on the Pilgrimage."
sentences.n: The edition prints لا سْتَأْذِنَكَ as two words. It is li-staʾdhinaka, "in order to ask your leave": the lām is the li- of purpose, the verb's opening alif has dropped out after it, and the result is split in the print. أَحُجَّ is the verb of the Pilgrimage itself (ḥajja).

sentences.t: فَمَنَعَهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ لَهُ اصْبِرْ إِلَى الْعَامِ الْقَابِلِ أَمْضِي أَنَا وَإِيَّاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-manaʿahu min dhālika wa-qāla lahu iṣbir ilā al-ʿāmi al-qābili amḍī anā wa-iyyāka
sentences.l: But he forbade him from that, and said to him: Be patient until the receiving year; I go, I and you.
sentences.i: But he forbade it, saying, "Wait until next year, and we shall go together, you and I."
sentences.n: أَمْضِي is the plain imperfect ("I shall go"), set down after the command without any linking word; Classical would more likely have the subjunctive or a wa-. الْعَامِ الْقَابِلِ, literally "the receiving year", is the usual way to say "next year".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْأَمْرَ يَطُولُ عَلَيْهِ دَخَلَ عَلَى أُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ فَوَجَدَهَا قَائِمَةً تُصَلِّي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-amra yaṭūlu ʿalayhi dakhala ʿalā ukhtihi Nuzhati al-Zamāni fa-wajadahā qāʾimatan tuṣallī
sentences.l: And when he saw the matter lengthening upon him, he entered upon his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and found her standing, praying.
sentences.i: Seeing that the matter was dragging on against him, he went in to his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān and found her standing in prayer.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَضَتِ الصَّلَوٰةَ قَالَ لَهَا إِنِّي قَدْ قَتَلَنِي الشَّوْقُ لِلْحَجِّ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ وَزِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ النَّبِيِّ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَوٰةُ وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaḍati al-ṣalāta qāla lahā innī qad qatalanī al-shawqu li-al-ḥajji ilā bayti Allāhi al-ḥarāmi wa-ziyārati qabri al-nabiyyi ʿalayhi al-ṣalātu wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: And when she had accomplished the prayer, he said to her: Indeed, the longing has killed me, for the pilgrimage to the House of God the Sanctified, and the visiting of the tomb of the Prophet, upon him the blessing and the peace.
sentences.i: When she had finished her prayer he said to her, "I am dying of longing for the Pilgrimage to the Sacred House of God, and to visit the tomb of the Prophet, on whom be blessing and peace."
sentences.n: قَتَلَنِي الشَّوْقُ, "longing has killed me", is an ordinary way to say "I am desperate for it". The word الصَّلَوٰة is spelled with a waw in the print, the old orthography for صلاة, so it carries the dagger alif above.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَأْذَنْتُ وَالِدِي فَمَنَعَنِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-istaʾdhantu wālidī fa-manaʿanī min dhālika
sentences.l: And I asked-leave of my father, and he forbade me from that.
sentences.i: I asked my father's leave, but he refused me.

sentences.t: فَالْمَقْصُودُ أَنْ آخُذَ شَيْأً مِنَ الْمَالِ وَأَخْرُجَ إِلَى الْحَجِّ سِرًّا وَلَمْ أُعَلِّمْ أَبِي بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-al-maqṣūdu an ākhudha shayʾan mina al-māli wa-akhruja ilā al-ḥajji sirran wa-lam uʿallim abī bi-dhālika
sentences.l: So the intended-thing (is) that I take something of the money and go out to the pilgrimage in secret, and not teach my father of that.
sentences.i: So my plan is to take some money and slip away on the Pilgrimage in secret, without letting my father know.
sentences.n: لَمْ أُعَلِّمْ is printed with a shadda, which makes it form II (ʿallama, "to teach"); Classical Arabic would say أُعْلِمْ (form IV) for "to inform". We keep the print's mark, and the bi- then marks what he is not telling his father about. سِرًّا, "in secret", is an accusative of manner.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أُخْتُهُ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا مَا أَصْحَبْتَنِي مَعَكَ وَلَا تَحْرِمْنِي مِنْ زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ukhtuhu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka illā mā aṣḥabtanī maʿaka wa-lā taḥrimnī min ziyārati qabri al-nabiyyi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: And his sister said to him: By God upon you, except that you take-me-as-companion with you, and do not deprive me of the visiting of the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace.
sentences.i: His sister said to him, "I beg you by God, take me with you, and do not deprive me of visiting the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace."
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ is an oath-plea, "I adjure you by God". After such an oath إِلَّا مَا does not mean "except"; it makes the request insistent: "you must take me along".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِذَا جَنَّ الظَّلَامُ فَاخْرُجِي مِنْ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَلَا تُعَلِّمِي أَحَدًا بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā idhā janna al-ẓalāmu fa-ukhruji min hādhā al-makāni wa-lā tuʿallimī aḥadan bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And he said to her: When the darkness grew-dark, go out from this place, and do not teach anyone of that.
sentences.i: He said to her, "When darkness falls, slip out of this place, and tell no one of it."
sentences.n: جَنَّ الظَّلَامُ is "the darkness closed in (covered over)"; the same verb gives jinn their name, the hidden ones. We point تُعَلِّمِي with the shadda, as the print does for the same verb just above.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ نِصْفُ اللَّيْلِ قَامَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَأَخَذَتْ شَيْأً مِنَ الْمَالِ وَلَبِسَتْ لُبْسَ الرِّجَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna niṣfu al-layli qāmat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni wa-akhadhat shayʾan mina al-māli wa-labisat lubsa al-rijāli
sentences.l: And when it was the half of the night, Nuzhat al-Zamān rose, and took something of the money, and put-on the wearing of the men.
sentences.i: At midnight Nuzhat al-Zamān rose, took some money, and put on men's clothes.
sentences.n: Here كَانَ is a full verb, "it came to be", so نِصْفُ اللَّيْلِ is its subject: "when midnight came". لُبْسَ الرِّجَالِ, literally "the wearing of the men", means their dress.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ قَدْ بَلَغَتْ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ مِثْلَ عُمْرِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَلَا زَالَتْ مَاشِيَةً إِلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat qad balaghat mina al-ʿumri mithla ʿumri Ḍawʾi al-Makāni wa-lā zālat māshiyatan ilā bābi al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And she had reached of age the like of the age of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and she did not cease walking to the gate of the palace.
sentences.i: She had reached the same age as Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and she walked on without a halt to the palace gate.
sentences.n: وَلَا زَالَتْ مَاشِيَةً is the verb زَالَ, "to cease", with a negative: "she did not cease walking", that is, "she kept on".

sentences.t: فَوَجَدَتْ أَخَاهَا ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ قَدْ جَهَّزَ الْجِمَالَ فَرَكِبَ وَأَرْكَبَهَا وَسَارَا فِى اللَّيْلِ وَاخْتَلَطَا بِالْحَجِّ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadat akhāhā Ḍawʾa al-Makāni qad jahhaza al-jimāla fa-rakiba wa-arkabahā wa-sārā fī al-layli wa-ikhtalaṭā bi-al-ḥajji
sentences.l: And she found her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān having equipped the camels; so he mounted and made her mount, and the two travelled in the night, and mingled with the pilgrimage.
sentences.i: She found her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān with the camels made ready; he mounted, set her up on a beast, and the two rode off through the night and mingled with the pilgrims.
sentences.n: الْحَجّ is used throughout for the body of pilgrims, the pilgrim caravan, as well as for the rite. In the print فِى is spelled with a dotless final ى here and with ي elsewhere; it is the same word. الْجِمَال is the plural of جَمَل, camel.

sentences.t: وَمَشَيَا إِلَى أَنْ صَارَا فِي وَسَطِ الْحَجِّ الْعِرَاقِيِّ
sentences.tr: wa-mashayā ilā an ṣārā fī wasaṭi al-ḥajji al-ʿirāqiyyi
sentences.l: And the two walked-on until they became in the middle of the Iraqi pilgrimage.
sentences.i: and they pressed on until they were in the midst of the Iraqi pilgrim caravan.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَا سَائِرَيْنِ وَكَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُمَا السَّلَامَةَ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَا مَكَّةَ الْمُشَرَّفَةَ وَوَقَفَا بِعَرَفَاتٍ وَقَضَيَا مَنَاسِكَ الْحَجِّ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālā sāʾirayni wa-kataba Allāhu lahumā al-salāmata ilā an dakhalā Makkata al-musharrafata wa-waqafā bi-ʿArafātin wa-qaḍayā manāsika al-ḥajji
sentences.l: And the two did not cease travelling, and God wrote for them safety, until the two entered Mecca the Ennobled, and stood at ʿArafāt, and accomplished the rites of the pilgrimage.
sentences.i: They travelled on without ceasing, and God decreed their safety, until they entered noble Mecca, stood at ʿArafāt, and performed all the rites of the Pilgrimage.
sentences.n: The print سائرين could be a plural, but the subject is two people, so we read the dual سَائِرَيْنِ ("travelling"). كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُمَا is "God decreed for them". The standing at ʿArafāt, on the ninth of Dhū al-Ḥijja, is the central rite of the Pilgrimage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَتَيَا لِزِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَزَارَاهُ
sentences.tr: thumma atayā li-ziyārati qabri al-nabiyyi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama fa-zārāhu
sentences.l: Then the two came for the visiting of the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, and visited it.
sentences.i: Then they came to visit the tomb of the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, and visited it,

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَرَادَا الرُّجُوعَ مَعَ الْحُجَّاجِ إِلَى بِلَادِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika aradā al-rujūʿa maʿa al-ḥujjāji ilā bilādihim
sentences.l: And after that the two wanted the return with the pilgrims to their lands.
sentences.i: and after that they wished to go home with the pilgrims to their own country.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لِأُخْتِهِ يَا أُخْتِي فِي خَاطِرِي زِيَارَةُ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ وَالْخَلِيلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Ḍawʾu al-Makāni li-ukhtihi yā ukhtī fī khāṭirī ziyāratu bayti al-maqdisi wa-al-khalīli Ibrāhīma ʿalayhi al-salāmu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his sister: O my sister, in my mind is the visiting of the House of the Holy-place and the Friend, Abraham, upon him the peace.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his sister, "My sister, I have it in mind to visit Jerusalem, and the Friend of God, Abraham, peace be upon him."
sentences.n: فِي خَاطِرِي, "in my mind", introduces a wish. بَيْتُ الْمَقْدِس ("the House of the Holy-place") is Jerusalem; الْخَلِيل, "the Friend" (of God), is Abraham's title, and in practice it also names Hebron, where he is buried, so the two visits are one journey.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَأَنَا كَذَلِكَ وَاتَّفَقَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-anā kadhālika wa-ittafaqā ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And she said to him: And I (am) likewise; and the two agreed upon that.
sentences.i: She said to him, "And so do I," and they agreed on it.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ وَاكْتَرَى لَهُ وَلَهَا مَعَ الْمَقَادِسَةِ وَجَهَّزَا حَالَهُمَا وَتَوَجَّهَا مَعَ الرَّكْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja wa-iktarā lahu wa-lahā maʿa al-maqādisati wa-jahhazā ḥālahumā wa-tawajjahā maʿa al-rakbi
sentences.l: So he went out, and hired for him and for her with the Jerusalemites, and the two prepared their condition, and turned-their-faces with the caravan.
sentences.i: So he went out and hired places for himself and her among the Jerusalemites, and when they had made themselves ready they set off with the caravan.
sentences.n: وَاكْتَرَى has no stated object: he hired (mounts, or passage) for the two of them, and the thing hired is understood. الْمَقَادِسَة is the plural of مَقْدِسِيّ, "man of Bayt al-Maqdis": the Jerusalemite pilgrims travelling home, with whom the pair now join.

sentences.t: فَفِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ حَصَلَتْ لِأُخْتِهِ حُمَّى بَارِدَةٌ فَتَشَوَّشَتْ ثُمَّ شَفَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-fī tilka al-laylati ḥaṣalat li-ukhtihi ḥummā bāridatun fa-tashawwashat thumma shafat
sentences.l: And in that night there occurred to his sister a cold fever, and she was-disturbed; then she was-healed.
sentences.i: That very night his sister was seized by a chill fever and fell sorely out of sorts; then she recovered.
sentences.n: حُمَّى بَارِدَة, "a cold fever", is a fever with shivering, a chill. شَفَتْ is printed without a yāʾ; we read shafat, "she recovered". Classical would say شُفِيَتْ ("she was healed"), and شَفَى normally takes an object, so this is a Middle Arabic use.

sentences.t: وَتَشَوَّشَ الْآخَرُ فَصَارَتْ تُلَاطِفُهُ فِي ضَعْفِهِ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا سَائِرَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-tashawwasha al-ākharu fa-ṣārat tulāṭifuhu fī ḍaʿfihi wa-lam yazālā sāʾirayni
sentences.l: And the other was-disturbed, so she became being-gentle-with him in his weakness, and the two did not cease travelling.
sentences.i: Then the other fell ill in turn, and she took to nursing him gently in his weakness, and they travelled on.
sentences.n: الْآخَر, "the other one", is Ḍawʾ al-Makān, taken ill after his sister. تَشَوَّشَ is "to be disturbed, upset", and here "to fall ill".

sentences.t: إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَا بَيْتَ الْمَقْدِسِ وَاشْتَدَّ الْمَرَضُ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَزَادَ مَعَهُ الضَّعْفُ
sentences.tr: ilā an dakhalā bayta al-maqdisi wa-ishtadda al-maraḍu ʿalā Ḍawʾi al-Makāni wa-zāda maʿahu al-ḍaʿfu
sentences.l: until they-two entered the House of the Holy-place, and the sickness grew-intense upon Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the weakness increased with him.
sentences.i: until the two of them reached Jerusalem, and the sickness pressed hard upon Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and his weakness grew with it.
sentences.n: بَيْتَ الْمَقْدِسِ, 'the House of the Holy-place', is the usual Arabic name for Jerusalem. The sentence finishes the journey begun in the previous one: the 'until' clause says where the two travellers have got to. ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ('Light of the Place') is the prince's name, and it is kept as a name in both English lines.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَا فِي خَانٍ هُنَاكَ وَاكْتَرَيَا لَهُمَا مَخْزَنًا فَنَزَلَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazalā fī khānin hunāka wa-iktarayā lahumā makhzanan fa-nazalā fīhi
sentences.l: So they-two alighted in a caravanserai there, and hired for themselves a storeroom, and they-two alighted in it.
sentences.i: They put up at a khan there, hired a storeroom, and took up their lodging in it.
sentences.n: خَانٌ is a caravanserai, an inn for travellers and their goods; a مَخْزَن is a storeroom, so they are renting the cheapest sort of space.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْمَرَضُ يَتَزَايَدُ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ حَتَّى انْحَلَّهُ وَغَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-maraḍu yatazāyadu ʿalā Ḍawʾi al-Makāni ḥattā inḥallahu wa-ghāba ʿani al-dunyā
sentences.l: And the sickness did-not cease increasing upon Ḍawʾ al-Makān until it dissolved him, and he was-absent from the world.
sentences.i: And the sickness never ceased to gain on Ḍawʾ al-Makān, until it wasted him away and he lost all awareness of the world.
sentences.n: The edition prints a shadda on انحلّه (the verb is inḥalla, "to dissolve, waste away", taking the object -hu); we keep it. غَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا, "he was absent from the world", means he lay unconscious or insensible, not that he died.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَمَّتْ لِذَلِكَ أُخْتُهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-ightammat li-dhālika ukhtuhu Nuzhatu al-Zamāni wa-qālat
sentences.l: So grieved on-account-of that his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and she said:
sentences.i: His sister Nuzhat al-Zamān was grieved at this, and she said:

sentences.t: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ هَذَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi hādhā ḥukmu Allāhi
sentences.l: No might and no strength except in God, the High, the Mighty; this is the judgement of God.
sentences.i: There is no might and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. This is God's decree.
sentences.n: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ is the stock formula of submission in the face of misfortune; the two nouns are accusative without tanwīn because lā negates the whole class.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَعَدَتْ هِيَ وَأَخُوهَا فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ وَقَلْ زَادَ بِهِ الضَّعْفُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qaʿadat hiya wa-akhūhā fī dhālika al-makāni wa-qal zāda bihi al-ḍaʿfu
sentences.l: So at that, she and her brother sat in that place, and qal the weakness had-increased in him.
sentences.i: So she and her brother stayed on in that place, and his weakness had grown still greater.
sentences.n: قَلْ is the print's spelling; the sense calls for قَدْ ("already, had") before the perfect زَادَ, so this looks like a misprint of the final letter (ل for د), and we point it as printed. The same slip recurs just below, in the brother's speech. زَادَ بِهِ الضَّعْفُ, with بِهِ, is literally "weakness increased in him".

sentences.t: وَهِيَ تَخْدُمُهُ وَتُنْفِقُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى نَفْسِهَا فَنَفِدَ مَا مَعَهَا مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya takhdumuhu wa-tunfiqu ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā nafsihā fa-nafida mā maʿahā mina al-māli
sentences.l: And she serving him and spending upon him and upon herself, so what was with her of the money ran-out.
sentences.i: She tended him and spent on him and on herself, until all the money she had with her was gone.

sentences.t: وَافْتَقَرَتْ حَتَّى لَمْ يَبْقَ مَعَهَا وَلَا دِرْهَمٌ
sentences.tr: wa-iftaqarat ḥattā lam yabqa maʿahā wa-lā dirhamun
sentences.l: And she became-poor until there did-not remain with her even a dirham.
sentences.i: She was reduced to poverty, until she had not so much as a single dirham left.

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلَتْ صَبِيَّ الْخَانِ إِلَى السُّوقِ بِشَيٍّ مِنْ قُمَاشِهَا فَبَاعَهُ وَأَنْفَقَتْهُ عَلَى أَخِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-arsalat ṣabiyya al-khāni ilā al-sūqi bi-shayyin min qumāshihā fa-bāʿahu wa-anfaqathu ʿalā akhīhā
sentences.l: So she sent the boy of the caravanserai to the market with a thing of her clothes, and he sold it, and she spent it upon her brother.
sentences.i: So she sent the inn's boy to the market with some article of her clothing; he sold it, and she spent the money on her brother.
sentences.n: The print writes شي for شَيْء ("a thing"), dropping the hamza letter, a colloquial spelling that recurs throughout this passage; we point it شَيٍّ and read it as "a thing, something".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَاعَتْ شَئْاً آخَرَ وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَبِيعُ مِنْ أَمْتِعَتِهَا شَئْاً فَشَئْاً حَتَّى لَمْ يَبْقَ لَهَا إِلَّاحَصِيرًا مُقَطَّعَةً
sentences.tr: thumma bāʿat shayʾan ākhara wa-lam tazal tabīʿu min amtiʿatihā shayʾan fa-shayʾan ḥattā lam yabqa lahā illāḥaṣīran muqaṭṭaʿatan
sentences.l: Then she sold another thing, and did-not cease selling from her goods thing by thing until there did-not remain to her except a mat, cut-up.
sentences.i: Then she sold another piece, and went on selling her belongings one thing after another, until nothing was left to her but a tattered mat.
sentences.n: الاحصيرا is printed as one run for إِلَّا حَصِيرًا ("except a mat"); we keep it as one word. The accusative after an exception with a negated verb is not Classical (which would say "nothing remained but a mat" with a nominative), and the feminine مُقَطَّعَةً for the masculine حَصِير is a further loose touch. شَيْئًا فَشَيْئًا means "little by little, one thing after another".

sentences.t: فَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ
sentences.tr: fa-bakat wa-qālat li-Allāhi al-amru min qablu wa-min baʿdu
sentences.l: So she wept and said: To God the command, from before and from after.
sentences.i: So she wept, and said, "The command belongs to God, before and after."
sentences.n: مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ ("before and after") is a Qurʾānic phrase (30:4). The edition prints the dammas on قبلُ and بعدُ, and we keep them: these two adverbs take the damma when their second term is left unsaid.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخُوهَا يَا أُخْتِي إِنِّي قَلْ حَسَسْتُ بِالْعَافِيَةِ وَفِي خَاطِرِي شَيٌّ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ الْمَشْوِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhūhā yā ukhtī innī qal ḥasastu bi-al-ʿāfiyati wa-fī khāṭirī shayyun mina al-laḥmi al-mashwiyyi
sentences.l: So her brother said to her: O my sister, I qal sensed well-being, and in my mind is a thing of roasted meat.
sentences.i: Then her brother said to her, "My sister, I feel that I have begun to mend, and I have a fancy in my mind for a little roast meat."
sentences.n: Again قَلْ stands where قَدْ is wanted ("I have felt…"); we point it as printed. حَسَسْتُ بِـ means "to sense, to feel" something. فِي خَاطِرِي ("in my mind") is the ordinary way to say that one has a notion or craving.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أُخْتُهُ وَاللَّهِ يَا أَخِي أَنَا مَالِي وَجْهٌ لِلشَّحَّاذَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ukhtuhu wa-Allāhi yā akhī anā mālī wajhun li-al-shaḥḥādhati
sentences.l: So his sister said to him: By God, O my brother, I — what is to me a face for begging?
sentences.i: His sister answered, "By God, my brother, I have no face for begging."
sentences.n: مَالِي is printed as one word (مَا لِي, "what is to me?" or "I have not"). Here it is best read as a flat negative, "I have no…"; وَجْه ("face") stands for the countenance one needs to beg, that is, the shamelessness.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ غَدًا أَدْخُلُ بَيْتَ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْأَكَابِرِ وَأَخْدُمُ فِيهِ وَأَعْمَلُ بِشَيٍّ نَقْتَاتُ بِهِ أَنَا وَأَنْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin ghadan adkhulu bayta aḥadin mina al-akābiri wa-akhdumu fīhi wa-aʿmalu bi-shayyin naqtātu bihi anā wa-anta
sentences.l: But tomorrow I will enter the house of one of the great-ones, and serve in it, and work for a thing we sustain-ourselves with, I and you.
sentences.i: But tomorrow I will go into the house of one of the great, and serve there, and work for something we can live on, you and I.
sentences.n: نَقْتَاتُ is Form VIII of قوت ("to feed oneself, subsist"), with بِهِ meaning "on it".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَفَكَّرَتْ سَاعَةً وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنِّي لَا يَهُونُ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أُفَارِقَكَ وَأَنْتَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ وَلَكِنْ أَرُوحُ قَهْرًا عَنِّي
sentences.tr: thumma tafakkarat sāʿatan wa-qālat lahu innī lā yahūnu ʿalayya an ufāriqaka wa-anta fī hādhihi al-ḥālati wa-lākin arūḥu qahran ʿannī
sentences.l: Then she thought for an hour and said to him: Indeed I — it is not easy upon me to part from you while you are in this state; but I will go, by-force, from me.
sentences.i: Then she thought for a while and said to him, "I cannot bear to leave you in this state; yet I must go, against my own wish."
sentences.n: قَهْرًا عَنِّي is obscure. قَهْرًا is "by force, perforce", and عَنِّي ("from me, on my part") most likely makes it "under compulsion, against my will". The print puts a shadda on عليّ, and we keep it. يَهُونُ عَلَيَّ means "it is easy for me", so with لَا, "I cannot bring myself".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخُوهَا أَبَعْدَ الْعِزِّ تُصْبِحِينَ ذَلِيلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhūhā a-baʿda al-ʿizzi tuṣbiḥīna dhalīlatan
sentences.l: So her brother said to her: What! After might, will you become abased?
sentences.i: Her brother said to her, "After such honour, will you end up humbled?"
sentences.n: The first alif is the question particle أَ, attached to بَعْدَ. تُصْبِحِينَ here simply means "you become".

sentences.t: فَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ ثُمَّ بَكَى وَبَكَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi thumma bakā wa-bakat
sentences.l: So no might and no strength except in God. Then he wept, and she wept.
sentences.i: "There is no might and no strength save in God." Then he wept, and she wept with him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا أَخِي نَحْنُ غُرَبَاءُ وَقَعَدْنَا هُنَا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً مَادَقَّ عَلَيْنَا أَحَدٌ الْبَابَ فَهَلْ نَمُوتُ مِنَ الْجُوعِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu yā akhī naḥnu ghurabāʾu wa-qaʿadnā hunā sanatan kāmilatan mādaqqa ʿalaynā aḥadun al-bāba fa-hal namūtu mina al-jūʿi
sentences.l: And she said to him: O my brother, we are strangers, and we have sat here a whole year, no one has knocked upon us the door; so shall we die of hunger?
sentences.i: And she said to him, "My brother, we are strangers here. We have sat in this place a whole year, and not one soul has knocked at our door. Are we to die of hunger?"
sentences.n: مَادَقَّ is printed as one word, مَا دَقَّ ("has not knocked"), and takes a direct object, الْبَابَ, together with عَلَيْنَا ("upon us"), which is the idiom "to knock at someone's door".

sentences.t: فَلَيْسَ عِنْدِي مِنَ الرَّأْيِ إِلَّا أَنِّي أَخْرُجُ وَأَخْدُمُ وَآتِيكَ بِشَيْءٍ نَقْتَاتُ بِهِ إِلَى أَنْ تَبْرَأَ مِنْ مَرَضِكَ ثُمَّ نُسَافِرُ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-laysa ʿindī mina al-raʾyi illā annī akhruju wa-akhdumu wa-ātīka bi-shayʾin naqtātu bihi ilā an tabraʾa min maraḍika thumma nusāfiru ilā bilādinā
sentences.l: So there is not with me of opinion except that I go out and serve, and bring you a thing we sustain-ourselves with, until you recover from your sickness; then we travel to our lands.
sentences.i: I have no plan but this: that I go out and work, and bring you something to live on until you are cured of your illness; then we shall travel home to our own country.
sentences.n: آتِيكَ بِشَيْءٍ is "I will bring you something": the verb أَتَى بِـ takes the thing brought with بِـ. The edition prints this one شيء with its hamza, unlike the shortened شي above. تَبْرَأَ مِنْ means "to recover from" (an illness).

sentences.t: وَمَكَثَتْ تَبْكِي سَاعَةً وَهُوَ يَبْكِي وَهُوَ مُتَّكِىًٔ
sentences.tr: wa-makathat tabkī sāʿatan wa-huwa yabkī wa-huwa muttakiʾan
sentences.l: And she stayed weeping an hour, and he weeping, and he reclining.
sentences.i: And she stayed weeping for an hour, while he too wept, propped on his side.
sentences.n: The print's متكىً is muttakiʾan, "reclining, leaning", a circumstantial accusative; the print writes the hamza-seat as ى and puts the tanwīn on it, and we keep that.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَغَطَّتْ رَأْسَهَا بِقِطْعَةِ عَبَاءَةٍ كَانَتْ مِنْ ثِيَابِ الْجَمَّالِينَ وَكَانَ صَاحِبُهَا نَسِيَهَا عِنْدَهُمَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni wa-ghaṭṭat raʾsahā bi-qiṭʿati ʿabāʾatin kānat min thiyābi al-jammālīna wa-kāna ṣāḥibuhā nasiyahā ʿindahumā
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān rose and covered her head with a piece of cloak which was of the garments of the camel-drivers, and its owner had forgotten it with the two of them.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān rose and covered her head with a piece of cloak that had belonged to some camel-drivers; its owner had left it behind with the two of them.
sentences.n: عَبَاءَة is the loose outer cloak. الْجَمَّالِينَ, "camel-drivers", are the muleteers or caravaneers who had stayed at the inn.

sentences.t: وَقَبَّلَتْ رَأْسَ أَخِيهَا وَاعْتَنَقَتْهُ وَخَرَجَتْ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي وَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَيْنَ تَمْضِي
sentences.tr: wa-qabbalat raʾsa akhīhā wa-iʿtanaqathu wa-kharajat min ʿindihi wa-hiya tabkī wa-lam taʿlam ayna tamḍī
sentences.l: And she kissed her brother's head and embraced him, and went out from beside him, she weeping, and she did not know where she would go.
sentences.i: She kissed her brother's head, embraced him, and went out from him weeping, not knowing where she was going.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَتْ سَائِرَةً وَأَخُوهَا يَنْتَظِرُهَا إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبَ وَقْتُ الْعِشَاءِ وَلَمْ تَأْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālat sāʾiratan wa-akhūhā yantaẓiruhā ilā an qaruba waqtu al-ʿishāʾi wa-lam taʾti
sentences.l: And she did not cease walking, and her brother awaiting her, until the time of supper drew-near, and she did not come.
sentences.i: She walked on without stopping, while her brother waited for her until suppertime drew near; and she did not come.

sentences.t: فَمَكَثَ أَخُوهَا يَنْتَظِرُهَا إِلَى أَنْ طَلَعَ النَّهَارُ فَلَمْ تَعُدْ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-makatha akhūhā yantaẓiruhā ilā an ṭalaʿa al-nahāru fa-lam taʿud ilayhi
sentences.l: So her brother stayed awaiting her until the day rose, and she did not return to him.
sentences.i: Her brother stayed waiting for her until the day broke, and she never came back to him.
sentences.n: Here Nuzhat al-Zamān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān are parted, and each will go his or her own way, not meeting again until much later in the tale.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ يَوْمَيْنِ فَعَظُمَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَهُ وَارْتَجَفَ قَلْبُهُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli yawmayni fa-ʿaẓuma dhālika ʿindahu wa-irtajafa qalbuhu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And he did not cease upon this state two days, and that grew-great with him, and his heart quaked over her.
sentences.i: He remained in this state for two days, and it weighed heavily upon him, and his heart trembled for her sake.
sentences.n: The subject is Ḍawʾ al-Makān, lying ill in the storeroom of an inn in Jerusalem; عَلَيْهَا, 'over her', is his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, from whom he has just been parted. لَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ 'he did not cease upon this state' is the ordinary way to say 'he stayed like this'; note that الْحَال is treated as masculine here, as it often is in later Arabic.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَدَّ بِهِ الْجُوعُ فَخَرَجَ مِنَ الْمَخْزَنِ وَصَاحَ لِصَبِيِّ الْحَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أُرِبْدَانْ تَحْمِلَنِي إِلَى السُّوقِ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtadda bihi al-jūʿu fa-kharaja mina al-makhzani wa-ṣāḥa li-ṣabiyyi al-ḥāni wa-qāla lahu uribdān taḥmilanī ilā al-sūqi
sentences.l: And hunger grew-severe with him, so he went-out from the storeroom and cried-out to the boy of the inn, and said to him: "I-want-that you carry me to the market."
sentences.i: Then hunger pressed hard upon him, and he came out of the storeroom and called to the inn's boy, and said to him, "I want you to carry me to the market."
sentences.n: اُرِبْدَانْ is a puzzle in the print: the letters spell uribdān, but the sense plainly asks for أُرِيدُ أَنْ 'I want that' (the yāʾ of أُرِيدُ replaced by a bāʾ, a misprint of a very easy kind). We point it as printed and translate what the sentence needs. الْحَان is the khan, the caravanserai or inn.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَهُ وَأَلْقَاهُ فِى السُّوقِ فَاجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْقُدْسِ وَبَكَوْا عَلَيْهِ لَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamalahu wa-alqāhu fī al-sūqi fa-ijtamaʿa ʿalayhi ahlu al-qudsi wa-bakaw ʿalayhi lammā raʾawhu ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati
sentences.l: So he carried him and threw him in the market, and the people of Jerusalem gathered about him and wept over him when they saw him in that state.
sentences.i: So the boy carried him and laid him down in the market, and the people of Jerusalem gathered round him and wept for him when they saw the state he was in.
sentences.n: الْقُدْس is 'the Holy (place)', the usual Arabic name of Jerusalem. The edition writes فِى, with an undotted final yāʾ, for fī; we read it as the ordinary preposition.

sentences.t: فَأَشَارَ إِلَيْهِمْ يَطْلُبُ شَيْأً يَأْكُلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ashāra ilayhim yaṭlubu shayʾan yaʾkuluhu
sentences.l: So he pointed to them, seeking a thing he might eat.
sentences.i: So he made signs to them, begging for something to eat.

sentences.t: فَجَاؤُا لَهُ مِنْ بَعْضِ التُّجَّارِ الَّذِينَ فِى السُّوقِ بِبَعْضِ دَرَاهِمَ وَاشْتَرَوْا لَهُ شَيْأً وَأَطْعَمُوهُ إِيَّاهُ ثُمَّ حَمَلُوهُ وَوَضَعُوهُ عَلَى دُكَّانٍ وَفَرَشُوا لَهُ قِطْعَةَ بَرْشٍ وَوَضَعُوا عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ إِبْرِيقًا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾū lahu min baʿḍi al-tujjāri alladhīna fī al-sūqi bi-baʿḍi darāhima wa-ishtarawā lahu shayʾan wa-aṭʿamūhu iyyāhu thumma ḥamalūhu wa-waḍaʿūhu ʿalā dukkānin wa-farashū lahu qiṭʿata barshin wa-waḍaʿū ʿinda raʾsihi ibrīqan
sentences.l: Then they came for him, from some of the merchants who were in the market, with some dirhams, and bought for him a thing, and fed him it; then they carried him and placed him upon a bench, and spread for him a piece of matting, and placed by his head a ewer.
sentences.i: Some of them went to the merchants of the market and came back with a few dirhams; they bought him something and fed him with it. Then they lifted him onto a shopfront bench, spread a piece of matting for him, and set a ewer by his head.
sentences.n: The sentence is loosely built: 'they came for him from some of the merchants with some dirhams' means they went to the merchants and returned with money. فَجَاؤُا is the print's spelling of فَجَاؤُوا (one wāw written where the verb has two letters' worth), and بِبَعْضِ دَرَاهِمَ leaves 'some dirhams' without the article. الدُّكَّان is the masonry bench in front of a shop.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ انْصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كُلُّ النَّاسِ وَحَمَلُوا هَمَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu inṣarafa ʿanhu kullu al-nāsi wa-ḥamalū hammahu
sentences.l: And when the night came on, all the people turned-away from him, and they carried his worry.
sentences.i: When night came on, all the people went away and left him, bearing his trouble with them in their hearts.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ نِصْفُ اللَّيْلِ تَذَكَّرَ أُخْتَهُ فَازْدَادَ بِهِ الضَّعْفُ وَامْتَنَعَ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ وَالشُّرْبِ وَغَابَ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna niṣfu al-layli tadhakkara ukhtahu fa-izdāda bihi al-ḍaʿfu wa-imtanaʿa mina al-akli wa-al-shurbi wa-ghāba ʿani al-wujūdi
sentences.l: And when it was the middle of the night, he remembered his sister, and weakness increased with him, and he refrained from eating and drinking, and became-absent from existence.
sentences.i: At midnight he remembered his sister, and his weakness grew worse; he would take neither food nor drink, and he lost all awareness of the world.
sentences.n: غَابَ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ, literally 'he was absent from existence', is the idiom for losing consciousness, not for dying. And الضَّعْف, 'weakness', is the subject of فَازْدَادَ بِهِ: it 'increased with him'.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَهْلُ السُّوقِ وَأَخَذُوا لَهُ مِنَ التُّجَّارِ ثَلٰثِينَ دَرَاهِمَ فِضَّةً وَاكْتَرَوْا لَهُ جَمَلًا وَقَالُوا لِلْجَمَّالِ احْمِلْ هَذَا وَأَوْصِلْهُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ وَأَدْخِلْهُ الْمَارَسْتَانَ لَعَلَّهُ يَبْرَأُ وَيَطِيبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ahlu al-sūqi wa-akhadhū lahu mina al-tujjāri thalāthīna darāhima fiḍḍatan wa-iktarawā lahu jamalan wa-qālū li-al-jammāli iḥmil hādhā wa-awṣilhu ilā Dimashqa wa-adkhilhu al-mārastāna laʿallahu yabraʾu wa-yaṭību
sentences.l: So the people of the market rose and took for him, from the merchants, thirty dirhams of silver, and hired for him a camel, and said to the cameleer: "Carry this one, and bring-him-to Damascus, and make-him-enter the hospital; perhaps he will recover and be well."
sentences.i: Then the market folk got up and collected for him, from the merchants, thirty silver dirhams, and hired a camel for him, and said to the camel-driver, "Take this man up and bring him to Damascus, and put him in the hospital; perhaps he will recover and be well."
sentences.n: ثَلٰثِينَ is printed ثلثين without the long alif, hence the dagger alif here; the count-construction (thirty + a plural, with 'silver' following) is loose, as often in this register. الْمَارَسْتَان is the hospital, from Persian bīmāristān; here it is the great hospital of Damascus, which is where the camel-driver is to take him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عَلَى الرَّأْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum ʿalā al-raʾsi
sentences.l: And he said to them: "On the head."
sentences.i: And he said to them, "Gladly, and with all my heart."
sentences.n: عَلَى الرَّأْسِ, 'on the head', is a stock phrase of ready compliance, much like 'consider it done': the order is placed on one's head, as a crown or a burden gladly borne.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الْجَمَّالُ فِي نَفْسِهِ كَيْفَ أَمْضِي بِهَذَا الْمَرِيضِ وَهُوَ مُشْرِفٌ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-jammālu fī nafsihi kayfa amḍī bi-hādhā al-marīḍi wa-huwa mushrifun ʿalā al-mawti
sentences.l: Then the cameleer said within himself: "How shall I go off with this sick-one, and he overlooking death?"
sentences.i: Then the camel-driver said to himself, "How can I go off with this sick man, when he is on the brink of death?"

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ بِهِ إِلَى مَكَانٍ وَاخْتَفَى بِهِ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ أَلْقَاهُ عَلَى مَزْبَلَةِ مُسْتَوْقَدِ حَمَّامٍ وَمَضَى إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja bihi ilā makānin wa-ikhtafā bihi ilā al-layli thumma alqāhu ʿalā mazbalati mustawqadi ḥammāmin wa-maḍā ilā ḥāli sabīlihi
sentences.l: So he went out with him to a place, and hid with him until the night, then threw him upon the rubbish-heap of the fire-place of a bathhouse, and went to the state of his way.
sentences.i: So he took him out to some place and lay hidden there with him until nightfall; then he dumped him on the rubbish heap by the furnace of a bathhouse and went his way.
sentences.n: مَضَى إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ, 'he went to the state of his way', is a fixed idiom for 'he went on his way'. الْمُسْتَوْقَد is the place where the fire is kindled, the bathhouse's stokehold.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ طَلَعَ وَقَّادُ الْحَمَّامِ إِلَى شُغْلِهِ فَوَجَدَهُ مُلْقًى عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu ṭalaʿa waqqādu al-ḥammāmi ilā shughlihi fa-wajadahu mulqan ʿalā ẓahrihi
sentences.l: And when the morning became morning, the fire-tender of the bath went up to his work, and found him thrown on his back.
sentences.i: When morning broke, the bathhouse stoker went off to his work and found him lying flung on his back.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ, 'the morning became morning', is a pleonastic formula that simply means 'day broke'. الْوَقَّاد is the man who lights and tends the fire, the stoker.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ لِأَىِّ شَيْءٍ مَايَرْمُونَ هَذَا الْمَيِّتَ إِلَّاهُنَا وَرَفَصَهُ بِرِجْلِهِ فَتَحَرَّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi li-ayyi shayʾin mā yarmūna hādhā al-mayyita illā hunā wa-rafaṣahu bi-rijlihi fa-taḥarraka
sentences.l: And he said within himself: "For what thing do they not throw this dead-one except here?" and kicked him with his foot, and he moved.
sentences.i: He said to himself, "Why must they always dump their dead on this very spot?" and gave him a kick with his foot, and the man stirred.
sentences.n: The print runs مَا and يَرْمُونَ together, and اِلَّا and هُنَا together (مايرمون, الاهنا); we keep each as one word. 'Why do they not throw… except here' means 'why is it always here that they throw…'. رَفَصَهُ is the print's spelling of رَفَسَهُ 'he kicked him', with ṣād for sīn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ الْوَاحِدُ مِنْكُمْ يَأْكُلُ قِطْعَةَ حَشِيشٍ وَيَرْمِي رُوحَهُ فِي أَيِّ مَوْضِعٍ كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu al-wāḥidu minkum yaʾkulu qiṭʿata ḥashīshin wa-yarmī rūḥahu fī ayyi mawḍiʿin kāna
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: "The one of you eats a piece of hashish and throws his soul in whatever place it be."
sentences.i: And the stoker said to him, "One of you fellows eats a lump of hashish and flings himself down wherever he happens to be."
sentences.n: The stoker takes the youth for a hashish-eater who has simply collapsed in the road; the next sentence shows him changing his mind. يَرْمِي رُوحَهُ, 'throws his soul', means 'throws himself down'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ فِي وَجْهِهِ فَرَآهُ لَانَبَاتَ بِعَارِضَيْهِ وَهُوَ ذُو بَهَاءٍ وَجَمَالٍ فَأَخَذَتْهُ الرَّأْفَةُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَرَفَ أَنَّهُ مَرِيضٌ وَغَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara fī wajhihi fa-raʾāhu lā nabāta bi-ʿāriḍayhi wa-huwa dhū bahāʾin wa-jamālin fa-akhadhathu al-raʾfatu ʿalayhi wa-ʿarafa annahu marīḍun wa-gharībun
sentences.l: Then he looked into his face, and saw him — no growth on his two cheeks — and he was possessed-of splendour and beauty; so pity seized him for him, and he knew that he was sick and a stranger.
sentences.i: Then he looked into his face and saw that it was beardless, with no down on the cheeks, and that the youth was one of radiance and beauty; pity for him took hold of him, and he understood that he was ill and a stranger.
sentences.n: لَانَبَاتَ is لَا نَبَاتَ run together in the print; 'no growth on his two cheeks' means he was beardless, no more than a boy. Here, and again in the next sentence, لَا is the negative of the whole class ('there is no …') and takes the accusative without tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ إِنِّي دَخَلْتُ فِي خَطِيئَةِ هَذَا الصَّبِيِّ وَقَدْ أَوْصَى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِإِكْرَامِ الْغَرِيبِ لَا سِيَّمَا إِذَا كَانَ الْغَرِيبُ مَرِيضًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi innī dakhaltu fī khaṭīʾati hādhā al-ṣabiyyi wa-qad awṣā al-nabiyyu ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama bi-ikrāmi al-gharībi lā siyyamā idhā kāna al-gharību marīḍan
sentences.l: And he said: "There is no might and no strength save in God. I have entered into the sin of this boy; and indeed the Prophet — God bless him and give him peace — commanded the honouring of the stranger, especially when the stranger is sick."
sentences.i: He said, "There is no might and no strength save in God! I have fallen into sin on this boy's account. The Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, enjoined honour to the stranger, and above all when the stranger is sick."
sentences.n: لَاحَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللَّهِ, 'there is no might and no strength save in God', is the formula of dismay or submission; the print runs each لَا onto its noun. The sin he speaks of is his own: he has just spoken harshly of a helpless stranger and kicked him. أَوْصَى بِـ means 'to charge someone with something', so بِإِكْرَامِ is 'with honouring…'.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَهُ وَأَتَى بِهِ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَدَخَلَ بِهِ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ وَأَمَرَهَا أَنْ تَخْدُمَهُ وَتَفْرُشَ لَهُ بِسَاطًا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamalahu wa-atā bihi ilā manzilihi wa-dakhala bihi ʿalā zawjatihi wa-amarahā an takhdumahu wa-tafrusha lahu bisāṭan
sentences.l: So he carried him and came with him to his house, and entered with him upon his wife, and commanded her that she serve him and spread for him a carpet.
sentences.i: So he picked him up and brought him home, and went in with him to his wife, and told her to wait on him and lay out a rug for him.

sentences.t: فَفَرَشَتْ لَهُ وَجَعَلَتْ تَحْتَ رَأْسِهِ وِسَادَةً وَسَخَّنَتْ لَهُ مَاءً وَغَسَلَتْ لَهُ بِهِ يَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ وَوَجْهَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-farashat lahu wa-jaʿalat taḥta raʾsihi wisādatan wa-sakhkhanat lahu māʾan wa-ghasalat lahu bihi yadayhi wa-rijlayhi wa-wajhahu
sentences.l: So she spread for him, and put under his head a pillow, and heated for him water, and washed for him with it his two hands and his two feet and his face.
sentences.i: She laid it out for him and put a cushion under his head; she warmed some water and washed his hands, his feet and his face with it.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجَ الْوَقَّادُ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأَتَى لَهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ مَاوِ الْوَرْدِ وَالسُّكَّرِ وَرَشَّ مَاءَ الْوَرْدِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَسَقَاهُ السُّكَّرَ وَأَخْرَجَ لَهُ قَمِيصًا نَظِيفًا وَأَلْبَسَهُ إِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaja al-waqqādu ilā al-sūqi wa-atā lahu bi-shayʾin min māwi al-wardi wa-al-sukkari wa-rashsha māʾa al-wardi ʿalā wajhihi wa-saqāhu al-sukkara wa-akhraja lahu qamīṣan naẓīfan wa-albasahu iyyāhu
sentences.l: And the stoker went out to the market, and brought for him some of the water of roses and sugar, and sprinkled rose-water upon his face, and gave him the sugar to drink, and brought out for him a clean shirt and clothed him in it.
sentences.i: The stoker went out to the market and fetched a little rose-water and sugar. He sprinkled the rose-water over the boy's face and gave him the sugar to drink, then brought out a clean shirt and dressed him in it.
sentences.n: The first time the word appears the print spells it مَاو, with a wāw in place of the hamza of مَاء; a few words later it is spelled مَاء in the ordinary way. أَتَى بِـ is 'to bring (something)'; the بِـ belongs to the verb, not to the thing.

sentences.t: فَشَمَّ نَسِيمَ الصِّحَّةِ وَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْعَافِيَةُ وَاتَّكَأً عَلَى الْمَخَدَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-shamma nasīma al-ṣiḥḥati wa-tawajjahat ilayhi al-ʿāfiyatu wa-ittakaʾa ʿalā al-makhaddati
sentences.l: And he smelled the breeze of health, and well-being turned toward him, and he reclined upon the cushion.
sentences.i: He caught the scent of returning health, wellbeing turned toward him, and he propped himself up against the cushion.
sentences.n: The print puts a tanwīn fatḥ on the final hamza of وَاتَّكَأً, which a perfect verb has no use for; it is most likely a stray mark for the plain fatḥa, and we keep it as printed.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْوَقَّادُ بِذَلِكَ وَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى عَافِيَةِ هَذَا الصَّبِيِّ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِسِرِّكَ الْمَكْنُونِ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ سَلَامَةَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ عَلَى يَدَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-waqqādu bi-dhālika wa-qāla al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi ʿalā ʿāfiyati hādhā al-ṣabiyyi Allāhumma innī asʾaluka bi-sirrika al-maknūni an tajʿala salāmata hādhā al-shābbi ʿalā yadayya
sentences.l: And the stoker rejoiced at that, and said: "Praise be to God for the well-being of this boy. O God, I ask You by Your hidden secret that You make the safety of this youth be upon my two hands."
sentences.i: The stoker was glad at this and said, "Praise be to God for this boy's recovery! O God, I ask You by Your hidden secret to let this young man's safety be worked through me."
sentences.n: بِسِرِّكَ الْمَكْنُونِ, 'by Your hidden secret', is an oath-like petition: he asks by God's concealed mystery. عَلَى يَدَيَّ, 'upon my two hands', is the usual way to say that something is accomplished through someone's agency. The pointing yadayya (dual with the first-person -ī) is ours; the print's يدي could equally be read yadī 'my hand'.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ————بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mu————bāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving off her permitted tale.
sentences.n: This is the closing formula of the night: 'the morning overtook Shahrazād and she fell silent from the permitted speech'. The print breaks the last word with a run of dashes (الم————باح); we read it as الْمُبَاحِ 'the permitted' and point it so, keeping the dashes where the edition has them.
